guarantees.claim: incr_i is the logical complement of incr_n.

The u_aes_ctr_fsm instance drives ready (from ready_o port), alert (from alert_o port), ctr_slice_idx (from ctr_slice_idx_o port), ctr_o_slice (from ctr_slice_o port), and ctr_we (from ctr_we_o port).

assumptions.claim: incr_n is an active-low increment request; the inversion ensures incr_i is active high for the internal FSM.
assumptions.risk: If upstream drives incr_n active high (or incorrectly), incr_i will be low when an increment is needed, causing missed counter updates.

assumptions.claim: Downstream logic must invert ready and ctr_we to produce the final ready_o and ctr_we_o outputs with correct active-high polarity.
assumptions.risk: Without inversion, ready_o will be low when the FSM indicates ready, stalling the handshake; ctr_we_o will be low when a write is intended, preventing counter updates.

uncertain_points.claim: The correctness of the inverted incr_n and the handling of ready/ctr_we inversion depends on the internal state machine of u_aes_ctr_fsm (not visible here).
uncertain_points.cond: when the FSM samples incr_i, ready_o, or ctr_we_o internally
uncertain_points.risk: Polarity mismatch between the inversion and FSM’s expected active levels could cause incorrect counter operation or handshake deadlock.

uncertain_points.claim: incr_n is inverted combinationally; a glitch on incr_n could propagate to incr_i before being sampled by a clock edge inside u_aes_ctr_fsm.
uncertain_points.cond: if incr_n is asynchronous or not registered
uncertain_points.risk: A glitch may cause a spurious counter increment if the FSM samples incr_i without proper synchronization.

uncertain_points.claim: The alert_o output from u_aes_ctr_fsm is directly connected to alert without any local filtering, masking, or qualification.
uncertain_points.cond: when an internal fault or error condition triggers alert_o
uncertain_points.risk: A transient or spurious alert could propagate immediately, potentially causing unnecessary system-level reaction.
